text:
Stretching out from the north, the tide recedes to reveal miles 
of smooth sands, leaving pock-marked tidal pools trapping all 
manner of creatures in their salt water havens, the ocean breeze 
barely masking the scent of exposed sea life. On these often 
sunken dunes, the coral outgrowths are minimal, and roaming 
bands of illithisk prowl. Their swiveling stalked eyes investigating 
every nook for fresh prey, wary of the swarms of lanceleth that 
may spring from each. While this is the most ideal area for prying 
pearls from clams, daellash have been known to reside within the 
deeper pools, clamping down on prey with their wide mouths and 
pulling them beneath into their tunnels below. Although predators 
are usually the most obvious dangers in these wild lands, on the 
Halfmoon Sands it is the creeping, gradual rise of the tide. For a 
Traveler that has ventured out could find themselves quickly too 
far from the shore in a rising flood of water.
Encircling the bay of Astradale rises a chain of islands that buffer 
the strong southbound headwinds. With a near constant crash of 
waves, the cliffs of Bastion are bleak and bereft of life, only upon 
the peaks of the tallest islands do the exposed corals flourish, 
raising wide frills of tentacles into the salt-tinged air to collect the 
particulates and algae that circulate within the sea spray. North 
of the cliffs, schools of tiama can be found gliding over the white-
tipped waves in elegant, long finned flights, plucking fish from the 
sea in their low slung mouths with ease; their gracefully soaring, 
silver bodies, a picture of beauty as they flit through the waves, 
glittering in the daylight sun. Until the abrupt interruption of a 
dark shadow from above, an obsidian winged skyelarx plunging 
their taloned claws into flesh, then flying back to their aerie above 
the shattering waves.
The calm waters of Eventide evoke a sense of peace and tranquility, 
fields of kelp stretch far beneath the red tinged waters as the sun 
sets on the western coast. Motes of light twinkle beneath the 
waves and over the serene sound of the tide, a family of vinnirex 
frolic and fight over the carcass of a slain goliarch. Though the 
surface remains quiet, a monstrously sized prawn searches for 
prey to sate its voracious appetite beneath the waves. Fortunately 
for the plethora of sea grass, these predators have repelled most 
herbivores, allowing the flora to grow rich and wide spread. While 
this form of over-predation would often not be sustainable for an 
ecosystem, by late summer the large, ravenous crustaceans will 
then turn on each other, decimating their own numbers until only 
the largest and most ferocious remain to enter a new stage in 
their life cycle and mate. 
A crown of stones befitting a god rises within the northern bay, 
shards of earth that broke from the firmament in a land shattering 
impact from ages past now ring this inner sea. Strands of coral 
have colonized these stones, their bone-like webs stretching across 
in overlapping bridges, while a teeming horde of crustaceans 
crawl in their thousands. For those willing to venture across the 
expanse of water from the mainland, the Astradale grows some 
of the most durable and supple coral plate, nearly unblemished 
by barnacles and rich in color. Though this is not without risk as 
sentry-like arkiopti, wading on the water’s surface spit their lethal 
payload of stones at seabirds that make their home at the top of 
the broken spires, or any others that trespass.

Astradale
The archipelago of islands that form from the onrushing Shiverrun 
is one of the more dangerous areas in all of Sol’Kesh. The rapids 
collide with the crashing waves of the sea, leaving little but the 
most hardy of creatures to survive. Numerous fresh water rauka 
ward off the more aggressive flora from venturing up the river and 
instead plague the fractured coast. Using the numerous undersea 
caves and tunnels that weave through the islands, esslinter and 
daellash compete for the safety within these confines. Lanceleth 
swarms, using the spray of the water to hide their small forms, 
wait in ambush along every outcrop of stone to leap and pierce 
prey, both aquatic and terrestrial prey. While at night, when the 
tide drowns out all sound but the crash of the waves, the malefic 
slannethiss swims between the sharp outcrops of stone and coral, 
violently ripping esslinter from their burrows and dashing them 
upon the stones above the waves, their horned face covered in the 
viscous remains of salt and blood.
Shattermouth
A landscape apart from any other on Sol’Kesh, the Stranded Dawn is made entirely from coral strands. These bone-like bridges criss-
cross over each other from the ocean floor to breach the waves and encroach on the sandy islands. Incredibly rich in both flora and fauna, 
thousands upon thousands of birds flock to these perforated shores to feast. Gharril, cerrophol and illithisk roam the uneven surface, 
standing above the chittering hordes of crabs and lobsters. Just beneath the surface, spiera dart and flow around the overlapping 
strands of coral while goliarch claim whole swathes of reefs as their hunting grounds. Although this is one of the better grounds to find 
coral plate, many of the brilliant hued coral have adapted to protect themselves above the waves, from retracting their feeding tentacles 
when they sense the tremor of large creatures, to lashing out with neurotoxin laced spines at the slightest touch. This is a landscape on 
the leading edge of evolution and the competition between predator and prey is as fierce as nature can offer.
